subject: Inconsistencies in files post-import to geomorph?

messages.author: 40e1914c9d91dcd7
messages.subject: Inconsistencies in files post-import to geomorph?
parts:
Hello all,

I'm very new to morphometric analysis and am trying to use a combination of TPS software and geomorph. Ultimately, I want to do a CVA or between-groups PCA to determine if there are significant shape differences between multiple insect species.

In tpsDig, I digitized landmarks and semilandmarks. In tpsUtil, I removed the control lines and made a sliders file for the semilandmarks. I can use tpsRelw to do the superimposition and view relative warps, consensus, etc... I used geomorph to import the TPS file (without control lines) and imported the sliders file using as.matrix(read.csv('filename.csv', header = T)). To get this to work, I added the "before, slide, after" header and deleted the 0 from the end of the first line. The generally procrustes analysis function completes with these two things and my consensus shape looks right (although the axes are reversed). However, the actual landmark values after import are very different than what was actually in the imported TPS file and the centroid sizes are also very different than those generated by tpsRelw.

Can someone explain to me why these are different (if this is normal) or what steps I might be doing wrong? I've attached a couple files to help explain what I'm talking about. Any help is appreciated!

messages.author: 91722721526eb1d7
messages.subject: Re: Inconsistencies in files post-import to geomorph?
parts:
Hi Te,

First of all - there's no need to modify the sliders file from TPSUtil, simply read in by:
sliders <- as.matrix(read.table('SampleSlidersOriginalTPS.tps', header = F, skip=2)) # where skip =2 skips the first two lines, and header is FALSE.

Your modified files are full of html formatting that is causing problems when reading them in with the geomorph readland functions so I cannot check them. I suggest if you do edit any text file, do so with a plan text editor like Notepad (windows) or text wrangler (mac).


Emma
